title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Past promotions at higher discounts show weak, noise-adjusted x1.0 lift; one recent week at same price sold 6 units (x1.94), but not consistent; price increase likely suppresses demand.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 3.1. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price increase to $5.72 (+3.4%) is notable, but past promotions show weak lift: median x1.15 vs baseline, noise-adjusted x1.0. The only recent price change (2026-09-28) had no uplift (x1.0). The classical model suggests no effect, and noise-adjusted evidence supports no meaningful promotion impact. The recent week (2026-10-05) at $5.72 sold 6 units (x1.94 vs baseline), but this may be noise. No post-promotion dip observed. Price increase likely suppresses demand; no evidence of demand shift. No driver justifies moving median from baseline. Confidence is low due to weak historical promotion signal and single price test.

TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15 (5 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.72 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.53)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.1 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 10.5 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 9.1

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-95% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
